supporting_evidence_verified: BP 160/87 mmHg on lisinopril 10 mg (uncontrolled stage 2 hypertension)
evidence_gaps: Serial BP measurements to confirm true resistance
Fasting glucose/HbA1c to complete metabolic‑syndrome criteria
concerns: Probability may be slightly low given the high prevalence of essential hypertension in this phenotype

evidence_gaps: Fasting plasma glucose, 2‑hour OGTT, or HbA1c
Serum insulin or HOMA‑IR if available
concerns: No direct glycaemic data; diagnosis rests on indirect markers

supporting_evidence_verified: Markedly elevated PDW (platelet activation linked to intermittent hypoxia)
concerns: Absence of symptom screen (snoring, daytime sleepiness) makes the diagnosis speculative

diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Secondary hypertension – primary aldosteronism / early CKD
supporting_evidence_verified: Possible low‑grade anemia (RBC 4.2 ×10⁶) suggesting chronic disease
evidence_gaps: Plasma renin activity and aldosterone levels
Serum creatinine/eGFR and urine albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio
concerns: No electrolyte or renin/aldosterone data; diagnosis remains speculative

diagnosis_verifications.diagnosis: Sub‑clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (high ASCVD risk)
supporting_evidence_verified: Low HDL‑C and borderline LDL‑C (atherogenic dyslipidaemia)
evidence_gaps: Coronary artery calcium score or carotid intima‑media thickness
concerns: Term “sub‑clinical ASCVD” is vague without imaging evidence
No hepatic labs or imaging provided

consistency_checks.detail: Recorded BP 160/87 while on lisinopril aligns with diagnosis of uncontrolled hypertension.
Low HDL and borderline LDL support metabolic‑syndrome and hypertension diagnosis.
PDW is attributed to OSA and inflammation but no diagnosis explicitly centres on platelet activation; a dedicated inflammatory diagnosis is missing.

top_concerns: Missing glycaemic data (fasting glucose/HbA1c) hampers confirmation of pre‑diabetes.
Renal function and electrolytes absent; secondary hypertension cannot be ruled out.
PDW elevation is unexplained by a specific diagnosis; needs repeat CBC and inflammatory work‑up.
Medication adherence and lifestyle factors (smoking, alcohol) not documented.
review_summary: The differential captures the core metabolic‑syndrome picture but under‑weights essential hypertension and omits key secondary‑cause considerations. Probabilities have been recalibrated, confidence scores assigned, and several evidence gaps highlighted. Additional work‑up for glucose, renal function, secondary hypertension, and sleep apnea is essential.
